followup_explanation:
This query is a well-specified technical task with clear completion criteria: build a neural network for stock price prediction given sample data. That's much closer to a structured, defined-output request than open-ended creative invention.

Willet-235B's top-rated tasks are exactly this kind of well-specified, criteria-driven work, and its capability profile on technical/instruction-following tasks (IFEval 85.3, strong MMLU-Pro) is right in line with Avocet's. The two models are effectively tied on the relevant capability dimensions, so I leaned on fit.

A couple of other small considerations: the slightly hostile tone ("Don't botch it like usual") is something Avocet self-reports an aversion to, whereas Willet shows near-zero slope on tone. That made Willet the cleaner match. (Note: task *preferences* are documented as dissociated from output quality, so this was a tie-breaker rather than a quality judgment — both models would perform comparably.)
